item.title: The IBM PC, Part 1: Arrival
item.description:
📝 In the early 1980s, the personal computer market was a raucous bazaar, teeming with variety. The problem was translating that knowledge into a product that would reach a mass audience. In 1973, IBM engineer Paul Friedel launched a single-user computer project that became the IBM 5100, a fifty-pound, all-in-one computer and terminal for scientists and engineers.
🔗 Read more: https://technicshistory.com/2026/07/24/the-ibm-pc-part-1-arrival/

item.title: Why is programming so captivating, yet so agonizing?
item.description:
📝 The first boundary is from program to product. Then the program must be thoroughly tested, so that one may trust it. A system component also costs at least three times as much as a standalone program with the same function.
🔗 Read more: https://elsewhere.news/en/zhenfund/why-is-programming-so-captivating-yet-so-agonizing

item.title: Game of Trees – Git-based version control from OpenBSD folks
How Do We Stop Vibe Coding?
item.description:
📝 Agents abstract away the code itself. It doesn't tell you that it's only going to implement something partially, or that it omitted something crucial that you assumed was obvious. The Solutions Are Immature We all understand that this is bad - but what about potential solutions.
